title: Think and Grow Rich
author: Napoleon Hill
tagline: The 13 steps to riches Hill drew from studying the most successful people of his time.
overview: Hill presents a philosophy of personal achievement built on 13 principles, from a burning desire and faith to organised planning, persistence and the 'master mind'. He argues that thoughts, backed by definite purpose and action, can be turned into material results.

chapters.title: Thoughts Are Things
chapters.summary: Hill opens with stories of people who achieved great things by fixing their minds on a definite goal and refusing to quit. His central claim is that thoughts mixed with definiteness of purpose, persistence and a burning desire tend to translate themselves into their physical equivalent.
keyIdeas: Many people quit just short of success.
chapters.tryThis: Write one goal in a single, specific sentence.

quiz.question: What does Hill say thoughts become when backed by purpose and desire?
quiz.explanation: He argues focused thought leads to real results.

chapters.title: Desire: The Starting Point of All Achievement
chapters.summary: Wishing isn't enough; you need a burning desire. Hill gives six steps: fix the exact amount you want, decide what you'll give in return, set a date, create a definite plan and start at once, write it all down, and read your statement aloud twice daily while picturing yourself already achieving it.
keyIdeas: A burning desire, not a wish.
Be exact about what and when.
Write and review your goal daily.
chapters.tryThis: Write your goal, what you'll give for it and a deadline; read it morning and night.

quiz.question: What does Hill say is the starting point of all achievement?
quiz.explanation: A definite, burning desire comes first.

chapters.title: Faith: Visualisation of, and Belief in, the Attainment of Desire
chapters.summary: Faith, for Hill, is a state of mind that can be cultivated through repeated instructions to the subconscious. By affirming your goals and acting as though they're achievable, belief grows — and belief drives the persistent action that achievement requires.
chapters.tryThis: Write a short confidence statement and repeat it daily for a week.

quiz.question: How does Hill say faith is developed?
options: Through repeated affirmation to the subconscious

chapters.title: Auto-Suggestion: The Medium for Influencing the Subconscious Mind
chapters.summary: Auto-suggestion means deliberately feeding your subconscious with thoughts, especially through daily, emotional repetition of your goals. Hill stresses that emotion and belief must accompany the words, and that this habit links desire and faith to the mind.
chapters.tryThis: Read your goal aloud with feeling every morning this week.

quiz.question: What makes auto-suggestion effective per Hill?

chapters.title: Specialized Knowledge: Personal Experiences or Observations
chapters.summary: General knowledge alone doesn't create wealth; organised, specialised knowledge applied toward a goal does. You don't need to know everything yourself — you can draw on others' expertise. Keep learning, and direct what you learn toward your purpose.
keyIdeas: Knowledge is power only when organised and applied.
chapters.tryThis: List the specialised knowledge your goal needs and where to get it.

quiz.question: What kind of knowledge creates results per Hill?
quiz.explanation: Knowledge must be applied to a definite end.

chapters.title: Imagination: The Workshop of the Mind
chapters.summary: Hill describes synthetic imagination, which rearranges existing ideas, and creative imagination, which produces new ones through inspiration. Ideas are where fortunes begin; imagination turns desire into plans.
keyIdeas: Two kinds of imagination: synthetic and creative.
Ideas are the beginning of fortunes.
chapters.tryThis: Spend 15 minutes brainstorming 10 ways to reach your goal.

quiz.question: What does synthetic imagination do?
options: Rearranges existing ideas into new combinations

chapters.title: Organized Planning: The Crystallization of Desire into Action
chapters.summary: Turn desire into action with definite plans, made with the help of a group of allies. If a plan fails, replace it with a better one — temporary defeat signals that the plan, not the goal, needs work. Hill also discusses qualities of leadership and common causes of failure.
keyIdeas: Temporary defeat means change the plan.
Lead well and avoid common failure causes.
chapters.tryThis: Write a step-by-step plan for your goal and pick the first step for tomorrow.

quiz.question: What should you do when a plan fails?
options: Replace it with a new plan
quiz.explanation: Defeat is a signal to adjust the plan.

chapters.title: Decision: The Mastery of Procrastination
chapters.summary: Hill found that successful people decide quickly and change their decisions slowly, while those who fail decide slowly and change often. Too much reliance on others' opinions breeds indecision; keep your own counsel and act.
chapters.tryThis: Make one decision you've been putting off, today.

quiz.question: How do successful people make decisions per Hill?
quiz.explanation: Promptness and firmness mark successful people.

chapters.title: Persistence: The Sustained Effort Necessary to Induce Faith
chapters.summary: Persistence is willpower sustained over time. It grows from a definite purpose, desire, self-reliance, definite plans, accurate knowledge, cooperation and habit. Hill lists signs of a lack of persistence and urges readers to build the habit deliberately.
keyIdeas: It can be built as a habit.
chapters.tryThis: Commit to one small daily action toward your goal for 30 days.

quiz.question: What does Hill say persistence can become?

chapters.title: Power of the Master Mind: The Driving Force
chapters.summary: A 'master mind' is a group of people working together in harmony toward a definite purpose. Their combined knowledge and effort create more than any individual could, and the group's energy multiplies each member's capacity.
chapters.tryThis: Invite two or three people to meet regularly to support each other's goals.

quiz.question: What is a master mind?
options: A harmonious group working toward a purpose

chapters.title: The Mystery of Sex Transmutation
chapters.summary: Hill argues that powerful drives and emotions can be redirected into creative and productive work. He claims many high achievers channel strong energy and enthusiasm into ambition and creativity rather than letting it scatter.
chapters.tryThis: Notice when you feel most energised and schedule your most important work then.

quiz.question: What is Hill's main idea in this chapter?
options: Redirect strong drives into productive work

chapters.title: The Subconscious Mind: The Connecting Link
chapters.summary: The subconscious works constantly on whatever dominates your thoughts. Hill urges filling it with positive emotions — desire, faith, enthusiasm — and keeping out negative ones like fear and jealousy, because both kinds cannot dominate the mind at once.
keyIdeas: The subconscious acts on dominant thoughts.
chapters.tryThis: List three positive emotions you'll focus on this week.

quiz.question: What does the subconscious act on?
quiz.explanation: What dominates your mind shapes action.

chapters.title: The Brain: A Broadcasting and Receiving Station for Thought
chapters.summary: Hill describes the mind as both sending and receiving ideas, suggesting that creative imagination can pick up inspiration and that stimulated minds — through desire and master-mind groups — produce more ideas.
keyIdeas: The mind both sends and receives ideas.
chapters.tryThis: Have an idea session with someone and capture every suggestion.

quiz.question: How does Hill describe the brain here?
options: A broadcasting and receiving station for thought
quiz.explanation: He likens it to sending and receiving ideas.

chapters.title: The Sixth Sense: The Door to the Temple of Wisdom
chapters.summary: The final principle, the 'sixth sense', is Hill's name for intuition and sudden insight. He says it develops only after the other principles are mastered, and describes imagining counsel from admired figures to sharpen judgment.
keyIdeas: It follows mastery of the others.
chapters.tryThis: Ask how a person you admire would approach your current challenge.

quiz.question: What does Hill call the 13th principle?

chapters.title: How to Outwit the Six Ghosts of Fear
chapters.summary: Hill identifies six basic fears that block success: poverty, criticism, ill health, loss of love, old age and death. He also warns about susceptibility to negative influences, urging readers to examine their fears and guard their minds.
keyIdeas: Name your fears to defeat them.
chapters.tryThis: Write which of the six fears affects you most and one step to counter it.

quiz.question: Which is one of Hill's six basic fears?
